Solving: models, incremental solving, cores and proofs

Source: vignettes/solving.Rmd
solving.Rmd
library(z3r)
ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_int(ctx, "y")

The three answers 

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x > 0, x < 3)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x > 0, x < 1)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "unsat"

The third answer, "unknown", means Z3 stopped without deciding. It is never a disguised "unsat":

z <- z3_int(ctx, "z")
s <- z3_solver(ctx, timeout = 300)
z3_add(s, x > 0, y > 0, z > 0, x^3 + y^3 == z^3)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "unknown"
z3_reason_unknown(s)
#> [1] "timeout"

Use timeout (milliseconds) or the deterministic rlimit to bound a check; Ctrl-C also interrupts one. z3_param_help(s) lists every solver parameter and z3_set_params() sets them with type checking:

z3_set_params(s, random_seed = 7, timeout = 1000)
z3_set_params(s, timeout = "soon")
#> Error:
#> ! parameter 'timeout' must be a non-negative whole number

Models 

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x + y == 10, x > 2 * y, y > 0)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
m <- z3_model(s)
m
#> <z3_model>
#>   y = 1
#>   x = 9
z3_eval(m, x * y)
#> <z3_expr Int> 9
z3_model_values(m)
#> $y
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $x
#> [1] 9

z3_eval() leaves constants the model does not mention symbolic, unless asked to complete the model:

w <- z3_int(ctx, "w")
z3_eval(m, x + w)
#> <z3_expr Int> (+ 9 w)
z3_eval(m, x + w, completion = TRUE)
#> <z3_expr Int> 9

A model belongs to one check. When the solver changes, z3r refuses to hand out a model until the next check, so a model never describes constraints it was not computed for:

z3_add(s, x > 100)
z3_model(s)
#> Error:
#> ! the solver has changed since the last z3_check(); call z3_check() again before requesting a model

The model already retrieved stays valid as a snapshot.

Models can also be built by hand, to evaluate formulas under chosen values:

m2 <- z3_model(ctx)
z3_model_set(m2, x, 4)
z3_model_set(m2, y, 7)
z3_eval(m2, x * y + 1)
#> <z3_expr Int> 29

Incremental solving

Push and pop scopes to explore variations without rebuilding the problem:

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x >= 0, x <= 10)
z3_push(s)
z3_add(s, x > 20)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "unsat"
z3_pop(s)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_num_scopes(s)
#> [1] 0

Assumptions hold for one check only:

z3_check(s, x == 3)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_check(s, x == 30)
#> [1] "unsat"
z3_assertions(s)
#> [[1]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> (>= x 0)
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> (<= x 10)

z3_with_scope() pops for you, even when the code inside fails:

z3_with_scope(s, {
  z3_add(s, x > 20)
  z3_check(s)
})
#> [1] "unsat"
z3_num_scopes(s)
#> [1] 0

Enumerating solutions

z3_all_models() lists distinct assignments of some variables by blocking each one found. The "status" attribute says whether all were found ("unsat"), the limit was reached, or Z3 gave up:

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x >= 0, y >= 0, x + 2 * y == 6)
sols <- z3_all_models(s, list(x, y))
do.call(rbind, lapply(sols, as.data.frame))
#>   x y
#> 1 0 3
#> 2 2 2
#> 3 4 1
#> 4 6 0
attr(sols, "status")
#> [1] "unsat"

Unsatisfiable cores 

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_assert_and_track(s, x > 10, "x_big")
z3_assert_and_track(s, x < 5, "x_small")
z3_assert_and_track(s, y == 2, "y_two")
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "unsat"
names(z3_unsat_core(s))
#> [1] "x_small" "x_big"

The core names a subset of the labelled constraints that is already contradictory; y_two is not in it. Cores are not guaranteed minimal. The same works with assumptions:

a <- z3_bools(ctx, c("a1", "a2", "a3"))
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, z3_implies(a$a1, x > 5), z3_implies(a$a2, x < 3), z3_implies(a$a3, y == 1))
z3_check(s, a$a1, a$a2, a$a3)
#> [1] "unsat"
names(z3_unsat_core(s))
#> [1] "a2" "a1"

Proofs

A context created with proof = TRUE records proofs of unsatisfiability:

pctx <- z3_context(proof = TRUE)
p <- z3_bool(pctx, "p")
q <- z3_bool(pctx, "q")
s <- z3_solver(pctx)
z3_add(s, z3_implies(p, q), p, !q)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "unsat"
substr(format(z3_proof(s)), 1, 200)
#> [1] "(mp (mp (asserted (=> p q))\n        (rewrite (= (=> p q) (or q (not p))))\n        (or q (not p)))\n    (trans (monotonicity (iff-false (asserted (not q)) (= q false))\n                         (monotoni"

Consequences, cubes and the trail

z3_consequences() reports which literals over chosen variables follow from the assertions and assumptions:

p <- z3_bools(ctx, c("p", "q", "r"))
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, z3_implies(p$p, p$q), z3_implies(p$q, p$r))
z3_consequences(s, list(p$p), list(p$q, p$r))$consequences
#> [[1]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> (=> p q)
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> (=> p r)

z3_cube() splits the search space for cube-and-conquer parallelism, and a simple solver (z3_solver(ctx, simple = TRUE)) exposes its decision trail:

s <- z3_solver(ctx, simple = TRUE)
z3_add(s, p$p, z3_or(p$q, p$r))
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_trail(s)
#> $literals
#> $literals[[1]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> p
#> 
#> $literals[[2]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> poly!36
#> 
#> $literals[[3]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> (not r)
#> 
#> $literals[[4]]
#> <z3_expr Bool> q
#> 
#> 
#> $levels
#> [1] 0 1 2 2

Validity: proving instead of finding

A formula is valid (true for every value) exactly when its negation is unsatisfiable:

prove <- function(ctx, formula) {
  s <- z3_solver(ctx)
  z3_add(s, !formula)
  switch(z3_check(s), unsat = "valid", sat = "not valid", unknown = "unknown")
}
prove(ctx, (x + y)^2 == x^2 + 2 * x * y + y^2)
#> [1] "valid"
prove(ctx, (x + y)^2 == x^2 + y^2)
#> [1] "not valid"

Logic-specific and tactic-based solvers 

s <- z3_solver(ctx, logic = "QF_LIA")
z3_add(s, 3 * x + 2 * y == 17, x >= 0, y >= 0)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
head(unlist(z3_statistics(s)), 6)
#>        propagations binary propagations        final checks           added eqs 
#>                   2                   2                   1                   1 
#>           mk clause    mk clause binary 
#>                   1                   2

z3_statistics_text() gives the same statistics as Z3 prints them.

Time limits and interruption

timeout limits one check to that many milliseconds; a check that runs out of time returns "unknown", and the solver keeps its own settings for the next check:

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x * x * x + y * y * y == 33, x > 0)
r <- z3_check(s, timeout = 50)
r
#> [1] "unknown"
if (r == "unknown") z3_reason_unknown(s)
#> [1] "timeout"

Inside a callback (vignette("propagators")), z3_interrupt(s) stops the running check, which then returns "unknown" with the reason "interrupted".

vignette("tactics") shows solvers built from tactics, and vignette("propagators") shows how R code can join the search.
